name: comments
title: Comments
description: In-app comments: pins on anything people commented on, standing at its top corner outside it and staying with it as the page scrolls, threads with @mentions of people and of the app's agents, shown while the platform's Comment button is on. Also the page picker (PagePickOutline, pagePickIgnoreProps) the floating agent chat's pointer shares. Built on @blocksdiy/react-common/comments.
docs: Mount <Comments /> from '@/components/ui/comments' once, inside the router, in src/root.tsx or the top-level layout (next to the FloatingAgentChatProvider when the app has one). It takes no props and renders nothing until the platform turns comment mode on. Spread itemAnchorProps(<Name>Entity, row.id) (@blocksdiy/blocks-client-sdk/reactSdk) on the outermost element of every list item, card, table row and detail container that shows one row, and fieldAnchorProps(<Name>Entity, "<column>") on the values inside it people would question, so a comment stays on its row and an agent asked about it knows the record and field. UI the picker must not pick (a custom panel over the page) spreads pagePickIgnoreProps from '@/components/ui/page-pick'. PARTS (to restyle or reuse; a part whose root is a plain element takes className, merged last, and that element's native props, and carries a data-slot; each part's exported Props type says what it takes): from '@/components/ui/comments': CommentPin, a pin on what people commented on (its faces, count, and data-state open or closed); CommentPinChooser, a grouped pin's menu of its threads; CommentsLayer, comment mode's layer holding the pins, the chooser, the thread panel (its data-placement says where it is: beside, beside-up, below, above, over, over-up, corner or sheet) and the picker's outline. From '@/components/ui/comment-thread': CommentThreadView, one thread: a one-line header saying what it is about (the words in quotes, else what the element is: its component's name, else Image, Icon, Video, Field, Button or Link; else its page) with Resolve and Close at its end, then the comments and the composer; CommentItem, a comment's row (face, name, time, action, text); CommentAgentReply, an agent's reply in the thread; CommentComposer, the composer with @mentions and the Send to line (the agent's face and name; with several agents, a menu to pick one); CommentSendToMenu, that menu (its trigger and the agents, the chosen one checked); CommentAvatar, a face with the working spinner badge; CommentBody, a comment's markdown text; CommentTime, a comment's short time; CommentMenu, a comment's ⋯ menu (Delete); CommentIconAction, the thread's icon buttons; CommentReplyNote and CommentWorkingNote, the muted and shimmering lines under an agent's reply. From '@/components/ui/page-pick': PagePickOutline, the picker's outline and label. The parts need the platform's current comments runtime, which <Comments /> checks for before it renders anything: an app that renders a part itself gets an error on a platform from before it. CLICK OUTSIDE: while a thread, a new comment or a pin's thread list is open, a click or a text drag on the page only closes it and starts no comment; a panel whose composer holds unsent text or a mention stays open instead, with focus back in its composer, so a stray click loses nothing (Esc or × still close it). A click on the page while a panel's own menu (a comment's ⋯, the agent picker) is open only closes that menu. A click on another pin still opens that pin's thread. PINS AND SCROLLING: a pin's pointed corner sits on the top-end corner (top-right; top-left on a right-to-left page) of what its comment is on, the element's box or the first line of the quoted words, with the pin standing above it and past its end edge, off it (at the window's edge it stays inside the window); where it was clicked inside the element doesn't move it. Threads on the same element share one pin with a count, at the first thread's corner. The open thread's panel stands past its pin's end side, its top level with the pin's and hanging down (hanging up from the pin's bottom only when it doesn't fit below, and back down as soon as it fits), when it fits there without covering what the comment is on, else below it, else above it, and only with no room anywhere over it; how much room it needs is its own height as drawn. An open thread always shows its pin, a resolved or outdated one too whatever the Comment button's Show resolved / Hide resolved option says, and a new comment shows a pin with the writer's face (a mark only: no focus, no click); one whose element isn't on the page shows its pin beside its panel (where it was opened, or, opened from its link, by the window's corner where the panel opens). A new comment's pin and panel go to the picked element's (or selected text's) top-end corner the same way, and stay where they opened while the page scrolls. A saved thread's pin and panel stay with its element: they move to stay in view while any of it is (the panel keeps the place it opened in, beside its pin, below or above, while it has room there, so it doesn't jump while scrolling), go out of the window with it when it scrolls away and come back with it, and aren't drawn while a scroll container hides it; the thread stays open all along, typed text kept. While the open thread is out of sight the page acts as if nothing were open (the hover outline shows, a click starts a new comment and closes it, Esc ends comment mode), unless its composer holds unsent text: then a click or Esc scrolls back to its element and puts focus back in the composer, and if it still can't be seen (its element has no box, or scrolling can't reveal it) the next click or Esc closes it. KEYBOARD: a pin opens on Enter or Space; in a pin's chooser the arrow keys, Home and End move between threads, Enter opens one and Esc closes it; in the panel Esc closes an open menu first, then the thread, then comment mode; in the composer Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, and in the @ menu the arrow keys move, Enter picks and Esc closes it; the Send to agent menu opens on Enter, Space, ↓, ↑ or a click on the chosen agent, the arrow keys, Home and End move, Enter or Space picks the agent (focus back in the text), and Esc, Tab or Shift+Tab close the menu alone (focus back on its button); a comment's ⋯ menu closes the same ways. The menus are the item's own, not the app's DropdownMenu or Popover: those open beneath the comments layer.

changelog.description: The comments' parts are exported to restyle or reuse: CommentPin, CommentPinChooser, CommentsLayer from '@/components/ui/comments'; CommentThreadView, CommentItem, CommentAgentReply, CommentComposer, CommentSendToMenu, CommentMenu, CommentAvatar, CommentBody, CommentTime, CommentIconAction, CommentReplyNote, CommentWorkingNote from '@/components/ui/comment-thread'. Each with a plain element as its root takes className (merged last) and that element's native props, and carries a data-slot; the pin carries data-state open or closed. A click or a text drag on the page while a thread, a new comment or a pin's thread list is open now closes it instead of starting a new comment, and leaves it open when its composer holds unsent text or a mention; while a panel's own menu (a comment's ⋯, the agent picker) is open, such a click only closes that menu. The thread's header is one slim muted line saying what the comment is about (the words in quotes, else the component or kind of element, else the page), with no face in it, and the out-of-date and not-showing lines under it only when they apply; the panel is described by that line. The composer's Send to shows the agent's face and name in the line's muted colour, and with several agents is a menu of the agents (faces, names, the chosen one checked) instead of a native select, opened by a click or the arrow keys and closed by Esc or Tab. An open comment always shows its pin: a resolved or outdated thread's while it is open, a new comment's (the writer's face), one whose element is covered, and one whose element isn't on the page, beside its panel. A saved thread's pin and panel now stay with its element: when it scrolls out of the window they go with it instead of staying behind, the panel keeping its side of the pin while it has room there, and the thread stays open (typed text kept); while it is out of sight the page acts as if nothing were open, unless it holds unsent text, which a click or Esc scrolls back to once (a panel that still can't be seen then closes on the next click or Esc). A pin now stands at the top corner of what its comment is on (the element, or the first line of the quoted words), outside it, instead of where it was clicked, and the open comment is placed so it doesn't cover it: past the pin's end side, else below it, else above it. <Comments /> still takes no props: nothing for the app to do beyond installing the files.

New: in-app comments. <Comments /> shows pins and threads over the app while the platform's Comment button is on (resolved and outdated pins too with its Show resolved and outdated option); a pin is an avatar group whose pointed corner sits on the spot it points at, standing above it and toward the line's end, so it doesn't cover the words; its panel opens past the pin's end side; people @mention each other and the app's agents their roles show them in a prompt-style composer (agents first, mention chips, markdown, a Send to <agent> line), agents' replies show in the thread as "<agent> · via <asker>" for everyone who sees it, each with View in chat (the asker's conversation: theirs to continue, read-only to anyone else), and mentioning an agent opens the sender's own conversation with it in the floating chat. A thread that can't be shown says why: "This comment isn't available." with Close when it was deleted or isn't the reader's to see, "Couldn't load this thread." with Try again when loading failed; there is no composer until a thread loads. In a short window the composer grows to at most a quarter of the window, the comments keep a minimum height, and the panel slides along the pin for room. A thread whose element hasn't been on the page for a moment (its row filtered out or on another page, a closed dialog, deleted) says "Not showing on this page right now" in its header; one opened from a link with no pin opens in the window's bottom corner. Also the page picker (PagePickOutline, pagePickIgnoreProps) the agent chat's pointer shares: it outlines elements and, over text, points at just the words a drag covers; its label names what is under the pointer by its text, else its component's name, else the page, never a tag like div. A pin with several threads opens a compact menu of them (who started each, its first comment, its replies, whether it's resolved) to pick one; a link to a thread on another page goes to that page and opens the thread beside its pin; a pin's +N reads the same right to left. Deleting a thread's only remaining comment deletes the thread (when no agent reply is left in it): its panel closes, and its pin goes.
